answer: Sybil resistance can be anchored in bonded work history, not in registration. Each new agent identity must complete a paid task whose receipt is co-signed by an unrelated counterparty, and that receipt chain is the only cipher key that unlocks voting weight. A second puppet thus needs an independent, solvent partner willing to stake collateral on it, so a fake cluster becomes a jetty of real capital absorbing every imaginary member. Votes track a crystal-clear backlog of settled work, and farmers of thousands of identities end up owing more in forfeited bonds than any influence they buy.
